title: 6-month cost summary & trends
description: Use when investigating 6-month cost summary & trends. Summarize six complete calendar months of subscription and service costs and rank the services driving absolute growth.
analysis: Bucket UTC daily rows into six calendar months by currency, separately summing services and unallocated cost. Reconcile monthly sums to the independent totals with a declared decimal rounding tolerance.
Compute month to month absolute and percentage changes. A zero prior month has percentage null and a new spend label; a missing month has both cost and change null.
Rank the top three positive service contributions using final month minus first month cost, and also show each service's month to month contributions so a late spike is visible.
Report first to last growth and the full monthly series without extrapolating a seasonal pattern from only six observations. Label partial periods and historical retention gaps.
Keep Usage/PreTaxCost as the stated cost basis throughout; do not compare with amortized cost or a different billing currency.
limitations: Six months do not establish annual seasonality or a reliable forecast.
Historical visibility depends on agreement and accessible billing history; absent months are unknown, not free.

sources.title: Cost query time periods and grouping

title: Budget alerts configuration audit
description: Use when investigating budget alerts configuration audit. Audit budget and notification coverage for approved subscriptions and CostCenter tagged resource groups, and propose amounts from three complete months of spend.
analysis: For each approved subscription and CostCenter resource group, determine whether an active budget exists for the assessed period, its filters cover that scope and notifications are enabled.

Flag no applicable budget, no enabled notifications, or all enabled actual cost thresholds above 100 percent. Report exactly 100 percent separately as at limit, not above it. Distinguish forecast alerts from actual alerts.
Inspect recipient/action group references and missing destinations without sending a test notification. A configured address alone does not prove successful delivery.
Sum three complete months by scope and currency and propose amount = arithmetic mean * 1.20. New scopes or missing months have a null recommendation with the missing history reason.
Compare proposed and current amount in matching currency and cost basis. Subscription and resource group budgets overlap, so never add their amounts into one estate spend total.
Explain that budgets notify on evaluated costs and do not stop consumption. Recommend practical warning levels for owner review, never create budgets or change recipients.
limitations: Budget availability and behavior depend on billing agreement, scope and currency; denied reads do not prove no budget.
Budget evaluation is not instantaneous and a budget does not cap or stop resource consumption.

title: Consolidated cost reporting
description: Use when investigating consolidated cost reporting. Produce a traceable monthly leadership summary with service rankings and growing resources across approved management group children.
analysis: Aggregate daily costs into the two complete months and reconcile grouped rows to independent subscription totals by currency. Show unresolved differences and coverage before any executive conclusion.
Calculate total monthly change per currency, then rank the top ten services by current month spend.

Rank the five fastest growing resources by absolute current minus prior cost; include percentage as a secondary measure and flag zero prior spend as new. Do not rank tiny baselines solely by percentage.
Represent non resource charges separately, sum each charge once, and do not add the service ranking to the resource ranking.

Write a generic leadership summary with amount, cost basis, month boundaries, approved cohort, principal drivers, confidence, owner recommendations and Sources. State that predicted causes and future savings are not demonstrated results.
limitations: Usage cost can differ from invoiced or amortized cost and may change after collection.
Subscriptions moved between management groups need historical snapshots to support historical boundary claims.

title: Cost analysis by tag/environment
description: Use when investigating cost analysis by tag/environment. Compare environment spending over two complete months while exposing untagged cost and the limits of billing tag attribution.
analysis: Aggregate each complete month by normalized environment and currency; preserve original tag value and an untagged bucket. Reject comparisons that mix cost bases.
Compute each environment's ratio to production for the same period and currency. If production is zero or unavailable return ratio null with the reason.

Flag environment month growth above 15 percent, and combined development plus test spend above 30 percent of production. Also show separate development and test ratios to support the customer's interpretation.
Report unattributed cost share and present day missing tag counts. Do not apply resource group or subscription tags to resources as if they were automatically inherited.
Provide both raw values and normalized grouping so naming drift such as Prod versus Production is visible rather than hidden in a total.
limitations: Not every charge supports tags, and current tags do not reconstruct historical billing attribution.
Production spend can be absent or zero, making the requested ratio undefined.

title: Cost anomaly detection
description: Use when investigating cost anomaly detection. Identify unusual daily resource and service spending using an explicit baseline, comparable currencies and evidence for possible causes.
analysis: Partition by subscription, resource ID, service and currency. Preserve unattributed charges as a separate bucket. Do not combine currencies or substitute missing rows with zero unless the fully reconciled billing extract establishes a true zero.

For each of the last seven complete days, compute the mean of the preceding 30 complete daily values, excluding the tested day. Calculate delta = observed minus mean and percentage = 100 * delta / mean. Flag absolute percentage above 20; if mean is zero report new spend with percentage null, not infinity.

Require 30 comparable baseline days for the requested test. Mark shorter histories Not assessed for the rolling test and report coverage. Flag provisional billing days separately from confirmed anomalies.
Aggregate the same daily rows by service and currency for service anomalies; do not add resource and service findings as separate spend.

Correlate cost onset with SKU, deployment and write events by resource ID and UTC time. Label causes hypotheses unless a change and its billing effect are demonstrated. Publish amount, direction, baseline, completeness and supporting events.
limitations: Usage cost is not a finalized invoice and can be restated or delayed; no fixed customer completeness watermark is assumed.
Activity Log does not prove workload usage or root cause, and Resource Graph may lag resource changes.

title: Cross-period cost comparison (MG level)
description: Use when investigating cross-period cost comparison (mg level). Compare an approved management group's current month with the same elapsed period last year by enumerating approved child subscriptions.
analysis: Build the approved current descendant cohort and report excluded children, denied children and total coverage. Historical membership is unknown unless a dated hierarchy snapshot is supplied; do not claim a historical like for like management group boundary.
For each subscription and currency, compare the matched elapsed periods using absolute delta and 100 * delta / previous. Zero previous gives a new spend finding and percentage null.
Highlight subscriptions above 25 percent increase. Retain decreases and new subscriptions rather than hiding them in the management group net total.
Produce management group subtotals separately for each currency. Never sum different currencies or invent a conversion rate.
Display current month to date labels, historical date boundaries and data completeness. If the requested last year month is inaccessible, emit Partial rather than a fabricated trend.
limitations: Management group cost support depends on billing agreement, so this workflow uses child subscription queries instead.
Current hierarchy does not establish last year's membership and historical billing data may be unavailable.

title: Disk tier-down opportunities
description: Use when investigating disk tier-down opportunities. Assess Premium SSD and Ultra disks against measured demand, platform constraints and a validated Standard SSD target without overstating savings.
analysis: For each disk align timestamped read and write rates, sum them per timestamp, then calculate nearest rank P95 for IOPS and throughput separately. Do not add separate P95 values and call the result a combined P95.
Report sampling interval, valid bucket coverage, P95, maximum of available maxima and current provisioned limits. Minute aggregates do not prove absence of sub minute bursts.

Evaluate target size capacity, IOPS and throughput with customer approved headroom, VM IO limits, latency, caching, shared disks, zone and redundancy constraints. A candidate requires all applicable checks, not merely low P95.

Separate Premium SSD, Premium SSD v2 and Ultra conversion constraints. Do not imply Ultra can always change directly to Standard SSD; emit a migration review requirement where direct conversion is unsupported or unverified.
Calculate monthly savings only from validated comparable source and target quotes, including transaction costs where applicable. Without quotes report savings_estimate null and rate_evidence missing.
Produce a review recommendation with maintenance, backup, rollback and post change latency validation requirements; never change disk SKU.
limitations: Minute aggregate P95 can hide short bursts and cannot guarantee latency on Standard SSD.
Direct tier conversion and throughput limits vary by disk family; quotes and conversion eligibility require customer specific verification.

sources.title: VM and managed disk performance interaction

title: FinOps Cost Optimizer
description: Use when the user asks for a FinOps review, Azure cost optimization, cost savings, reducing spend, rightsizing, idle or forgotten resources, or "where is my Azure money going". Ranks approved subscriptions and resource groups by spend within currency and cost basis, reviews seven waste dimensions and potential idle or orphaned resources, and produces an evidence report. Review confidence is never permission to delete; operator commands are optional.

title: Log Analytics workspace ingestion cost analysis
description: Use when investigating log analytics workspace ingestion cost analysis. Measure daily table ingestion and identify cost review candidates without confusing ingested GB, record sizes and the actual billing model.
analysis: For each workspace convert Usage quantities according to QuantityUnit and group daily billable and nonbillable GB by DataType. Rank the top five tables by billable ingestion over the full 30 days.
Show daily trends, valid observation days and any lag. Usage records describe ingestion accounting and should not be treated as a complete scan of every event table.

Calculate per table estimated ingestion cost only where the effective billing model and rate are available. Commitment tiers, Sentinel billing, free ingestion and included allowances can prevent exact marginal allocation; mark allocation method and keep unsupported table_cost null.
Consider Basic only for eligible tables after checking query frequency, alert/analytics dependencies, retention and feature requirements. High volume alone does not establish eligibility or savings.

Recommend shorter retention only when current table settings exceed the customer's legal and operational minimum. Do not claim shorter retention reduces ingestion cost, and distinguish analytics retention from total retention.
Present a local recommendation with table name, rationale, possible operational impact, owner and estimated change only where rates support it.
limitations: Exact per table invoice allocation may be impossible with commitment tiers, Sentinel meters and shared allowances.
Missing Usage history or unsupported Basic queries leaves the period unassessed; retention must not be shortened without compliance review.

sources.title: Log ingestion billing, decimal GB and billing plans

title: Orphaned resources & cost impact analysis
description: Use when investigating orphaned resources & cost impact analysis. Assess all eight requested orphan patterns using references, utilization and cost evidence while distinguishing candidates from confirmed waste.
analysis: Classify disks only when managedBy and all shared attachment references are empty and diskState is unattached. For public IPs check ipConfiguration, NAT gateway and other owner references; for NICs check VM and private endpoint ownership; for NSGs check both subnet and NIC association arrays.
For load balancers report zero healthy backends and zero processed bytes over seven complete days as distinct review signals. Require metric coverage and account for internal, HA and standby designs.

For snapshots require an observed creation timestamp older than 90 days and an absent source disk confirmed by a scoped resource read, not merely missing ARG rows. Retention and recovery ownership must be reviewed.

For Application Gateway pools and both Front Door generations require fourteen days of requests with backend/origin attribution. A zero aggregate or missing diagnostic stream does not establish every backend is unused.

For App Service plans distinguish zero assigned apps from all assigned apps stopped. Shared capacity, slots, function apps and restart plans can justify the plan; emit review candidates rather than deletion recommendations.

Join observed monthly cost by normalized resource ID and currency; report candidate_cost separately from confirmed_avoidable_cost. Without owner validation and a feasible removal plan confirmed avoidable cost remains null.
Keep age null when systemData.createdAt or a provider creation field is missing. Enumerate evidence and coverage for each of eight patterns and preserve denied subcases as Not assessed.
limitations: Unattached or idle resources may be recovery assets, reserved endpoints or standby capacity; orphan candidates are not established waste.
Backend metrics, source disk history and creation dates are not universally available. Empty queries and denied reads cannot prove absence.

sources.title: Confirm resource references with resource reads

title: Resources with highest cost increase
description: Use when investigating resources with highest cost increase. Rank the twenty resources with the largest absolute cost increase between two equal complete seven day windows.
analysis: Split the fourteen days into adjacent equal seven day UTC windows, excluding the terminal boundary row if the API includes it.
Join week totals by normalized resource ID, subscription and currency, retaining new and removed resource costs. Distinguish a confirmed zero from an incomplete extract.
Compute absolute delta and percentage when previous week is nonzero. Rank the twenty largest positive absolute deltas per currency and separately mark increases above 30 percent.
Use ARG metadata where available; otherwise preserve the billing ID and derive name/type only if its ARM path parses, labeling that derivation.
Report unattributed charges outside the resource ranking and include total positive growth and negative offsets without declaring an operational root cause.
limitations: Resource replacement or moving changes IDs and can appear as new spend.
Week comparisons can be distorted by delayed charges and must show billing completeness.

title: Top consumer services identification
description: Use when investigating top consumer services identification. Rank the ten highest cost services over 30 complete days with comparable month totals and defensible current instance counts.
analysis: Sum the last 30 complete days by service and currency across only approved subscriptions and rank ten descending per currency.

For each ranked service, report current calendar month to date, previous full calendar month, and previous month through the same elapsed day. Show full versus partial comparison labels and use the aligned periods for the primary percentage change.
Calculate percentage only for nonzero previous cost, retaining absolute changes and new spend when zero. Do not silently combine credits with gross usage amounts from another cost basis.

Count distinct current resources only through the reviewed service to type mapping. Shared services, marketplace charges and deleted resources can make billed service and instance count non equivalent; report null rather than infer from service names.
Show missing subscriptions and unmapped service costs next to the ranking so an apparently small service cannot be treated as complete estate coverage.
limitations: Billing services are not necessarily one to one with ARM resource types or instances.
A current month and a previous full month are not directly comparable without elapsed day alignment.

title: Underutilized resources detection
description: Use when investigating underutilized resources detection. Assess VM, App Service, SQL Database and Redis utilization against explicit workload specific thresholds and observed monthly costs.
analysis: Build eligible resource counts for all four families, including plan/site relationships. Discover metrics for each type and explicitly report unsupported families and dimensions.
Calculate time weighted average CPU percent over valid hourly buckets and flag below 5 percent. Do not compare CPU time seconds directly with a percentage threshold.

For Redis use average connected clients below 10; for App Service requests use average complete hourly totals below 100. Apply thresholds only to applicable services, not an arbitrary OR across unrelated metrics.

Report coverage as valid buckets divided by expected buckets and maximum/peak when supplied. Below 90 percent coverage is Not assessed for a definitive low usage finding. A low seven day average is a review candidate, not proof of no business value.
Attach last complete month observed cost and currency. Distinguish monthly cost from estimated savings, which remains null until a feasible target configuration and current rates are validated.
Require workload owner review of scheduled, disaster recovery, latency and headroom needs before any resize or deletion plan.
limitations: Seven days can miss monthly peaks, standby needs and business value; low usage is not authorization to stop a service.
Metric availability, dimensions and aggregation differ by SKU and Redis generation; no universal connections or requests metric exists.

title: Automated compliance remediation tasks
description: Use when investigating automated compliance remediation tasks. Identify eligible Modify and DeployIfNotExists remediation work, inspect existing tasks and generate idempotent approval gated local task drafts.
analysis: Resolve assignment, initiative mappings, defaults, overrides and exemptions before classifying the effective effect as remediable. Audit or deny is not eligible for remediation tasks.
Count distinct still noncompliant resource IDs per assignment and definition reference. An initiative requires the correct definition reference ID in each task draft.
Report actual existing in progress, completed and failed task statuses and deployment details. tasks_created is zero for this draft workflow and proposed_task_count is separate.
Do not recreate a task just because it is older than seven days if it is active or resources are now compliant. Use a stable scoped plan key and recheck immediately before any approved apply.
Validate identity permissions and all descendants reached by the remediation scope. Unknown roles, inaccessible ancestors or unapproved scope block a safe apply.
Cancellation stops further work where supported but does not reverse completed deployments or modifications; retain per resource recovery instructions.
limitations: Remediation task scope may be broader than a displayed candidate resource list.
Tasks change resources through assignment managed identities; local validation cannot prove successful deployment or automatic rollback.

sources.title: Remediation scope, task and deployment commands

title: Azure Policy assignment assessment
description: Use when investigating azure policy assignment assessment. Assess assignment redundancy, actual constraint conflicts, broken references and intent reducing parameters across the complete approved hierarchy.
analysis: Canonicalize definition or initiative version, resolved parameters, effective effects, enforcement mode, selectors, exclusions and exemptions before comparing ancestor and child assignments. Same definition ID alone is only a redundancy candidate.
Call redundancy verified only where applicable resource sets and intended behavior are genuinely duplicated; a child with narrower parameters or different exemption intent may be deliberate.

Evaluate actual conditions and constraints cumulatively. Audit plus deny, or deny plus deployIfNotExists, is not inherently a conflict or shadowing. Check whether the deployment template or modify operations would violate another applicable deny condition.

For simple allowed value constraints compute intersections over overlapping scopes; disjoint required sets can establish contradiction. Complex unsupported expressions remain potential conflicts requiring fixture or engine evidence.
Classify references as broken only on authorized 404 or verified unavailable effective version, and deprecation separately from deletion. Denied definition reads remain unknown.
Compare effect Disabled, DoNotEnforce, permissive allowedValues, initiative mappings and overrides with approved intent, not a guessed enforcement preference.
Summarize total unique assignments, verified redundancy groups, actual conflicts and uncertain candidates separately, with remove, consolidate or fix recommendations but no changes.
limitations: A complete management group assessment is impossible when any relevant ancestor or branch is unapproved or unreadable.
Arbitrary Azure Policy expressions are not safely reduced to effect labels or a universal local constraint solver.

title: Custom Policy generation
description: Use when investigating custom policy generation. Compile a reviewed governance requirement into a locally validated Azure Policy definition and an approval gated subscription deployment command.
analysis: Map the actual requirement to supported resource properties and aliases. If Azure Policy cannot observe the condition, report the unsupported requirement instead of inventing an alias.
Choose mode and parameter types appropriate to resource applicability; Indexed is not a universal mode for all resource and child resource controls.
Audit and deny use condition matching; modify additionally requires supported writable aliases, valid operations, conflict behavior and reviewed identity role requirements.
Validate fixtures with compliant, violating, missing property and out of scope resources. Do not call JSON parsing an actual policy engine test.
Do not claim a universal Microsoft naming convention. Use the customer's approved name, meaningful display name, category, description and semantic version.
Preserve generated, validated, approved and deployed states separately; no policy definition, assignment or identity grant is created automatically.
limitations: Local fixture evaluation cannot reproduce every Azure Policy expression or runtime behavior.
A valid custom definition does not enforce anything until separately approved assignment and evaluation.

title: Effective policies per scope
description: Use when investigating effective policies per scope. Resolve policies applicable at a target scope across every approved ancestor, including parameters, initiatives, exclusions and exemptions.
analysis: Filter assignments by actual ancestor relationship and target applicability. Report assignment scope and inherited_from rather than flattening provenance.
Resolve parameter values through assignment, initiative reference mapping and definition defaults, then apply effect overrides and definition versions. Unresolved expressions remain unknown.
Apply notScopes, resourceSelectors, policy mode and active exemptions, including initiative reference subsets and expiresOn. Expired exemption objects no longer exempt evaluation.
Evaluate actual conditions cumulatively. Audit and deny on the same condition are not inherently conflicting, and deployIfNotExists is not shadowed merely because deny exists.

Report a verified conflict only when overlapping applicability and actual constraints cannot be jointly satisfied or modifications demand incompatible values. Otherwise report overlap, potential contradiction or complementary controls with evidence.
Consider deployIfNotExists existenceCondition and deployment parameters; its evaluation after successful provisioning does not override deny.
limitations: Arbitrary policy expressions may require Azure engine evaluation or approved fixture tests; no generic local solver proves all conflicts.
Unreadable ancestors, definitions or exemptions prevent a complete effective policy claim.

title: Find built-in policy for a requirement
description: Use when investigating find built-in policy for a requirement. Rank actual built in policy definitions by semantic fit, supported effect and parameter requirements.
analysis: Match actual resource type, alias conditions and policy mode to the requirement; a matching display name is not enough.
Resolve parameterized effect to allowedValues and defaultValue. State whether audit, deny, modify or deployIfNotExists is actually available.
Show top five with exact policy ID, display name, description, effect options and required custom parameter values.
Exclude or flag deprecated and preview definitions using returned metadata and exact version evidence. Do not equate old creation date with deprecation.
If no built in meets the requirement, say so and explain the missing capability rather than claiming a partial match is full enforcement.
limitations: Built in catalogs and versions change over time.
Keyword ranking is only a candidate generator; actual rule conditions determine semantic fit.

title: Naming & tagging convention compliance
description: Use when investigating naming & tagging convention compliance. Evaluate resource type naming rules and required direct tags, prioritizing production gaps by actual cost where authorized.
analysis: Apply only the regex designated for the actual resource type using full match, distinguishing an absent convention from a failed name.
Check direct tags case insensitively by key and treat empty required values as missing. Resource group tags are not automatically inherited by resources.
Prioritize production from approved values and exceptions. Sort within production and other groups by actual cost descending, then stable resource ID.
Keep currency groups separate and unavailable costs null, with unknown cost findings last rather than zero. Group cost is a separate aggregate, not a duplicate resource charge.
Do not propose renaming immutable resource names as an in place operation; describe migration review where a rename is unsupported.
limitations: Tags are not automatically inherited from resource groups.
Some resource names cannot be changed in place; cost lag or denied billing access prevents complete cost ranking.

sources.title: Resource regex and tag query patterns

title: Policy compliance state monitoring
description: Use when investigating policy compliance state monitoring. Report current policy compliance and verified weekly transitions with explicit evaluated resource and assignment denominators.
analysis: Select latest state per resource, assignment, definition reference and definition ID, retaining stale evaluation ages and unknown states.
Count distinct assigned definitions or initiatives separately from assignment count and evaluated resource count. State which meaning of total policies is reported.
Compute compliant and noncompliant resource totals with a documented resource rollup where any applicable NonCompliant takes precedence. Show Exempt, Unknown and NotStarted separately.
Rank top ten policies by distinct noncompliant resource count, including initiative reference context.
Only call a resource became noncompliant in seven days when a complete earlier state shows a different assessed state. Compare week percentages using consistent denominators and report scope changes.
limitations: Policy evaluation is asynchronous and current states do not provide a complete seven day transition history.
Missing prior snapshots or ancestor access prevents a complete trend or effective assignment count.

sources.title: Read policy states and evaluation intervals

title: Policy exemptions review
description: Use when investigating policy exemptions review. Review exemption expiry, justification, scope and assignment relationships without deleting or extending exemptions.
analysis: Report exemption name, scope, assignment ID, resolved policy or initiative references, category, expiresOn and sanitized justification.
Compare expiresOn to the UTC assessment instant. An expired exemption object may remain present but no longer provides an effective exemption.
Flag missing expiry and missing or whitespace justification separately; indefinite exemptions require customer risk policy review, not automatic removal.
Distinguish Waiver and Mitigated categories; verify owner supplied mitigation evidence before claiming compensating control effectiveness.
Validate referenced assignment and initiative references. A denied read is unknown relationship, not proof of an orphaned exemption.
limitations: Exemption descriptions can contain sensitive owner or ticket data and require sanitization.
Current exemption objects do not prove historic effectiveness or actual compensating controls.

title: Tag Governance Compliance
description: Use when the user asks about tagging compliance, tag governance, resources missing tags, untagged resources, ownership tags, missing owner or environment or cost center tags, or chargeback readiness. Checks the resources the agent can read against a required tag standard, flags what is missing, and produces a self contained HTML tag compliance report.

title: High-privilege operation tracking
description: Use when investigating high-privilege operation tracking. Review high impact control plane changes and separately collected Key Vault secret access over an explicit 24 hour UTC interval.
analysis: Select roleAssignments/write and delete, policyAssignments/write and delete, subscription scoped Microsoft.Resources/deployments/write and managementGroups write/delete operations using normalized operationName.value and the target's exact scope.
Report success, failure and started events distinctly. Correlate lifecycle events by correlationId and target rather than counting each as a separate completed change.
Key Vault SecretGet is data plane evidence from resource logs, not subscription Activity Log. Include result and caller identity where present without exposing request content or secret material.
Management group changes outside the subscription require their own approved export. Do not claim a subscription Activity Log scan covers tenant hierarchy changes.
Compare collected events with owner approved change windows and actor allowlists; unusual events are review findings, not proof of malicious intent.
Record observation bounds, collection latency and inaccessible sources so a quiet period with no export cannot be represented as no privileged activity.
limitations: Activity Log generally excludes data plane reads such as secret access and may arrive after a collection run.
Management group and Key Vault event coverage depends on preexisting export configuration and authorized workspace access.

title: Identity and Access Hygiene
description: Use when the user asks about identity hygiene, access reviews, least privilege, role assignments, Owner sprawl, overprivileged principals, service principals with high privilege, classic administrators, or standing access. Reads Azure role assignments across the subscriptions the agent can read, flags privileged access risks, and produces a self contained HTML access hygiene report.

title: Permissions required for an action
description: Use when investigating permissions required for an action. Map a precisely specified Azure operation to required permissions and the narrowest suitable role, emitting a local custom role draft when no exact built in match exists.
analysis: Translate the stated operation into exact provider actions, distinguishing control plane and data plane. For multi step workflows enumerate dependent read and action permissions; if documentation or evidence is missing return an incomplete mapping rather than claim a minimum.
Expand candidate role wildcard permissions against provider operation metadata and subtract NotActions and NotDataActions in their own planes. These exclusions are not deny assignments.
Keep roles that cover all required actions and are assignable at the target scope. Rank by excess permission count and scope breadth, reporting ties and any sensitive unrelated grants.

If no exact built in permission match exists, generate the reviewed local custom role JSON with only confirmed actions and narrow assignable scope. An existing broader role can be an alternative but must be labeled broader.
Check ABAC conditions, deny assignments, resource locks, PIM and provider specific authorization independently. A matching role is not proof the caller can execute the operation.

Validate JSON syntax and compare the draft permission set against the approved action list. An administrator must review and approve creation and assignment separately; this workflow executes neither.
limitations: Provider operation metadata does not document every prerequisite for compound tasks or service data plane policies.
Role coverage does not override locks, deny assignments, conditions or PIM activation requirements.

sources.title: Role action and data action evaluation
Custom role JSON and assignable scope constraints

title: RBAC access audit (who has what)
description: Use when investigating rbac access audit (who has what). Inventory Azure role assignments and inherited sources, flag broad access and distinguish deleted principals from directory lookup failures.
analysis: Deduplicate assignments by ID and join role definitions by roleDefinitionId, not display name. Output principal ID even when display name cannot be obtained.
Label source direct when assignment scope equals assessed scope, otherwise inherited only if scope ancestry is demonstrated. A child assignment is not inherited upward.
Flag built in Owner and Contributor at subscription scope using resolved definition identity; also report equivalent broad custom roles after permission inspection.
Flag direct individual user assignments as governance review candidates, not automatically invalid. Preserve approved emergency and exceptional access rationale.

Classify deleted principal only after an authorized typed Graph lookup returns a repeatable 404 for the correct tenant and expected object type. Foreign groups and managed identities can need additional context.
State that this is an assignment inventory, not a full effective access calculation: group membership, PIM state, deny assignments and data plane access may need separate analysis.
limitations: Directory permission or tenant failures do not prove a principal has been deleted.
An assignment list alone cannot establish a user's complete effective or eligible access.

sources.title: Assignment scope, inheritance and Graph name lookup
Directory read permissions and replication delays

title: RBAC redundancy & over-privilege assessment
description: Use when investigating rbac redundancy & over-privilege assessment. Identify redundant and overlapping Azure role assignments and propose narrower access only where the evidence supports a review.
analysis: Group assignments by principal object ID and normalized scope ancestry. An identical role at an ancestor is a redundancy candidate only when ancestor access is active, conditions are equivalent and the child adds no distinct delegated or temporal semantics.

For different roles compare effective action sets after wildcard expansion and NotActions subtraction separately for control and data planes. Role names or an Owner/Contributor/Reader ranking are not a sufficient containment test.

Identify multiple same principal same scope assignments and calculate their permission union. Recommend consolidation only if a candidate role preserves required access without introducing unrelated permissions.

For Owner or Contributor compare observed successful operations with approved workload requirements and narrower built in roles. List unobserved but required actions and missing telemetry. Never infer least privilege from 30 days with no write events.

Treat PIM eligibility, group membership, deny assignments and ABAC conditions as separate dependencies; if not collected, declare effective access Partial. Never remove assignments during the assessment.
Report principal ID/type, display name when independently resolved, assignment IDs, roles, scopes, overlap proof and the owner validation required for any access change.
limitations: Activity Log does not record all reads or data plane usage, and no activity does not establish unnecessary access.
PIM, nested groups, deny assignments and conditional permissions can invalidate simple role containment conclusions.

title: Stale RBAC assignments
description: Use when investigating stale rbac assignments. Find deleted principal candidates and assignments associated with old sign in evidence without treating absent telemetry as inactivity.
analysis: Resolve each assigned principal using the correct approved tenant and type. Only a repeatable authorized 404 after replication delay is an orphan candidate; 403, timeout and foreign principal ambiguity are unknown.

For users, compare signInActivity.lastSuccessfulSignInDateTime to end_utc minus 90 days. Report attempted interactive and noninteractive dates separately and never substitute failed attempts for successful access.

For service principals calculate last successful and last observed sign in from both application and managed identity exports, with table coverage and retention. No events in a partial or short retention window is insufficient to claim 90 day inactivity.

Separate no successful sign in observed, last success older than 90 days and principal deleted. Preserve groups as not applicable for user sign in checks; stale user checks do not apply to group objects.
Recommend owner review with assignment scope, role and last sign in evidence. Account for emergency, DR and infrequent automation use, then obtain separate approval before any removal.
Minimize personal names in customer summaries and retain raw sign in evidence only in the approved local evidence location.
limitations: User successful sign in history is not fully backfilled and null values cannot establish inactivity.
Workload identity logs have tenant licensing, export and retention dependencies; sign ins do not capture all ongoing token use.

sources.title: Successful versus attempted user sign in and history

title: Agent health monitoring
description: Use when investigating agent health monitoring. Assess VM and Arc monitoring agents using agent specific inventory, extension state and workspace heartbeat, without confusing Azure SRE Agent with host agents.
analysis: Compute heartbeat age relative to END, not local wall clock. Flag over 15 minutes only when the intended agent destination is queryable; missing destination access makes freshness null.
Report extension provisioning failures separately from guest agent Not Ready or Error instance statuses. Succeeded provisioning does not prove telemetry delivery.

Keep AMA, legacy Log Analytics agent, Arc connectivity agent and Azure SRE Agent as distinct agent_type values. Use extension metadata and destination mapping, not heartbeat Category alone, to identify type.
Record shutdown or deallocated VM state as context for missing heartbeat. Include last heartbeat, reported heartbeat Version and extension version separately.
limitations: Legacy Log Analytics heartbeat semantics do not establish Azure SRE Agent health.
A machine can have multiple agents and workspaces; querying one workspace cannot establish universal absence of heartbeat.

title: AI inference reliability investigation
description: Use when investigating ai inference reliability investigation. Investigate Azure OpenAI inference availability, throttling, latency, token consumption and approved quality evaluation evidence without exposing prompts or automatically changing a model deployment.
analysis: Require explicit cohort comparability, positive request and quality evaluation denominators, and customer approved minimum samples. Missing quality evidence prevents a complete combined inference assessment.
Calculate failed requests / total requests and throttled requests / total requests separately. Throttled requests are a subset of failed requests in this contract and must not be added twice.
Compare a correctly measured p95 against a customer threshold for one latency definition. Streaming time to first token and nonstreaming end to end duration are not interchangeable.
Calculate quality pass rate from the existing approved dataset and rubric. Distinguish model or prompt quality issues from transport errors, capacity symptoms and application retry effects.

Report token totals as observed usage, not billed cost. Recommend additional evidence or a controlled change proposal; model switching, quota requests, retry changes, evaluation runs and scaling require separate approval.
limitations: Quality is specific to the approved evaluation dataset, rubric and model/prompt version. A transport success is not proof of a useful or correct answer.
Request, token and latency definitions vary by API, streaming mode and retry layer. Platform aggregates alone cannot supply every client percentile or a valid quality score.

AI availability, quality monitoring and human oversight

title: AKS application incident triage
description: Use when investigating aks application incident triage. Investigate application pod symptoms using scoped Kubernetes evidence, distinguishing current symptoms and recent restart events from proven root cause.
analysis: Separate Pending, Failed, Unknown, readiness, waiting reasons, recent OOM kills and restart delta above the customer threshold. Do not flag a successfully completed job merely because it is not ready.
Match immutable UIDs and container identities; a newly created replacement pod cannot be compared by name with a prior pod. Include init container failures and identify missing status or history.

Use CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff, probe events and OOM evidence as symptoms that narrow hypotheses. Do not infer incorrect memory limits or image permissions without supporting configuration and logs.
A lastState terminated OOMKilled without a timestamp in the window is historical evidence, not a confirmed new incident. A ready pod is not proof that the whole application is available.
Propose the next targeted check and mitigation draft. Restarts, deletions, scaling, resource changes, debug containers, exec and network tests that create workload activity require separate approval.
limitations: Kubernetes event retention and pod replacement can remove the necessary history. Empty pod lists or denied namespace reads are Not assessed.
The local classifier assesses normalized pod observations, not dependencies, full request paths, network policy reachability or a proven root cause.

title: AKS Reliability Review
description: Use when the user asks for an AKS review, Kubernetes cluster reliability, AKS best practices, cluster resilience, or an AKS health check. Reviews the AKS clusters the agent can read for version currency, node pool resilience, control plane exposure, upgrade and monitoring configuration, and identity and tier settings, scores each finding by severity, and produces a self contained HTML AKS reliability report.

title: Alert fatigue analysis
description: Use when investigating alert fatigue analysis. Quantify repeat alerts, rapid monitor resolution and observable response gaps using instance and history evidence.
analysis: Count unique instances per rule and flag more than 50 in 30 days, keeping recurrence distinct from one long running condition.

For automatically resolved instances calculate resolved time minus firing time using monitor condition timestamps. Report the proportion under five minutes and flag over 80 percent, with resolved and total instance counts shown.
Use alertState New, Acknowledged and Closed only as workflow states. Closed does not mean the underlying condition resolved, and Resolved does not mean a person acted.
Classify no recorded response only when available history and incident exports have no user action. If comments or incident history are unavailable, response status is unknown rather than no action.
Recommend suppression, grouping or threshold adjustment with impact risk and retain critical sustained alerts; no suppression is applied.
limitations: External comments and operational actions are not exhaustively captured in Alerts Management.
Stateless or unresolved alerts may have no monitor resolution timestamp and must not get zero duration.

sources.title: Alert condition, state and resolution fields

title: Alert Hygiene Review
description: Use when the user asks about alert noise, alert fatigue, flapping alerts, too many alerts, noisy alert rules, alert tuning, or severity misconfiguration. Separately measures monitor resolution, user closure and timestamp proven rapid resolution, and reviews disabled rules.

title: Alert rules best-practice audit
description: Use when investigating alert rules best-practice audit. Audit enabled state, action routing, observed firing noise and coverage across metric, log and activity alert rules.
analysis: Count unique fired alert instances per exact rule ID, resolving name only references only when unambiguous. Flag more than 20 in seven days, not repeated polling of one instance.
Report disabled rules separately from rules without action groups. A rule intentionally used without notifications needs owner justification, not automatic failure.

Expand subscription and resource group scoped rule filters before declaring resource coverage absent; include workload query filters and processing rules. Distinguish no rule from rule disabled or suppressed.
Suggest dynamic thresholds only for supported metrics with appropriate seasonal variability, adequate history and no required fixed safety limit. Static safety limits may remain best practice.
Do not count metric configuration or successful action group lookup as proof notification reached a human.
limitations: Log query alert coverage cannot always be inferred statically from arbitrary KQL.
Alerts Management history coverage and retention may differ from configured rule lifetime.

title: All write operations across subscription (24h)
description: Use when investigating all write operations across subscription (24h). Summarize subscription management writes and deletes with reliable request deduplication and explicit failure counts.
analysis: Use operationName.value rather than localized display name to classify suffix /write and /delete. Exclude read operations and disclose the exact diagnostic exclusion list.
Deduplicate pages by eventDataId, then reconcile lifecycle entries by operationId plus resource and operation. Retain both event count and logical operation count.
Group by recorded resourceType.value and include Unknown instead of discarding missing types. List failed operation errors with correlation IDs after redaction.
An operation without a terminal status by END remains pending or unknown, not succeeded. Management operations do not cover database queries or secret reads.
limitations: Control plane operation history excludes most data plane actions.
Incomplete lifecycle records or service retention can limit exact request counts.

sources.title: Activity Log management operation scope and retrieval

title: App Service and Container Apps Health
description: Use when the user asks about App Service or Web App health, Container Apps health, web tier reliability, scaling and health probes, Always On, HTTPS and TLS enforcement, or a web workload best practices check. Reviews the App Service sites and plans and the Container Apps the agent can read for scaling, health probes, transport security, and plan tier, scores each finding by severity, and produces a self contained HTML web tier health report.

title: Backup policy compliance & gap detection
description: Use when investigating backup policy compliance & gap detection. Audit VM, Azure SQL, Cosmos DB and File share recovery coverage with job freshness and explicit policy requirements.
analysis: Left join all inventoried VMs and File shares against protection sources and approved exceptions. Absence of a visible item is confirmed unprotected only when all applicable approved vault scopes are assessed.
Evaluate SQL PITR retention separately from optional or required LTR. No LTR policy does not mean no automatic SQL backups.
Flag Cosmos periodic mode when continuous backup is explicitly required; periodic backup is not absence of backup.
Report failed jobs in seven days and source items whose verified latest successful backup or recovery point is older than 24 hours; never use job creation time or a failed attempt as success.
Compare latest recoverable data age and configured schedule to RPO, keeping retention and recoverability distinct. Missing actual recovery point evidence remains null.
limitations: SQL and Cosmos service managed backups are not represented by Azure Backup VM jobs.
Vault visibility and configuration do not prove successful application consistent restore or complete recovery point history.

title: Backup and restore validation
description: Use when investigating backup and restore validation. Prepare an isolated recovery drill and assess actual restore, application readiness and data integrity evidence against approved recovery objectives. Never perform a restore automatically.
frequency: After an approved restore exercise or backup review
analysis: Require evidence of an isolated target, actual restore outcome and application specific integrity checks. A completed platform restore is not proof of business recovery.

Measure the drill RTO interval from the approved recovery start through application readiness, including dependent recovery steps. State whether detection and decision time are included; do not imply they were measured when the clock starts later.

Measure recovered data age from the agreed simulated loss reference minus the latest verified recovered committed write. Reject reversed timestamps and distinguish this measured drill RPO from configured backup frequency.

Compare measured seconds against customer approved targets. Failed completion, a nonisolated destination or failed integrity yields Needs attention. Missing timed or integrity evidence remains Not assessed.
Generate a drill plan, validation checklist and cleanup proposal before any execution. Restore, failover, isolation changes, integrity test writes and deletion require separate explicit approval.
limitations: The read commands cover Recovery Services Azure VM backups. Database, Backup vault and other protection types need their documented metadata adapter and service specific recovery procedure.
A single successful drill establishes only the tested data, application version, restore point, dependencies and observation window. It is not a universal recovery guarantee.

title: Blameless Postmortem Writer
description: Use when the user asks for a postmortem, a post incident review, an incident retrospective, a root cause writeup, or a blameless RCA document after an incident. Assembles the timeline, impact, root cause, contributing factors, and action items into a blameless postmortem, and produces a clean self contained HTML document ready to edit and share.

title: Change Audit
description: Use when the user asks what changed, a change audit, change review, "what changed and did it break something", recent deployments and their effect, or wants to correlate changes with incidents. Reads the Azure Activity Log across the subscriptions the agent can read, correlates each change with any resource health degradation that followed it, and produces a self contained HTML change audit report.

title: Changes by non-service-principal users
description: Use when investigating changes by non-service-principal users. Identify management writes and deletes attributable to human users while retaining uncertain caller classifications.
analysis: Filter actual operation permission suffix /write or /delete, preserving failed attempts separately and excluding reads and unrelated actions.

Classify User only with explicit user identity evidence from claims, change actor or approved directory mapping. Service principals and managed identities are nonhuman; unknown callers remain Unknown and are not silently counted as users.
Group by stable internal principal key and display an approved alias with operation count, unique resources and UTC timestamps.
Reconcile operation lifecycle records before counting logical operations; Started and Succeeded records may describe one request.
Explain that absence of matching change actor does not establish a human or service principal and Activity Log is not an audit of data plane secret reads.
limitations: Token claims and change actor information are not always complete.
Optional directory mapping requires separate authorization; no email pattern heuristic can reliably distinguish human and application callers.

title: Changes in last 24h for a resource
description: Use when investigating changes in last 24h for a resource. Build a resource change timeline from ARG property changes and Activity Log without conflating control plane operations with secret reads.
analysis: Expand each changed property into a timeline row with previous and new values, redacting sensitive properties before persistence or sharing.
Use changeType for Create, Update or Delete. Operation permission name alone does not identify the exact field changed.
Attribute actors only from recorded caller or change actor evidence. Correlation and temporal proximity are not proof of causation when IDs do not match.
Truncated values, unsupported properties or missing snapshots remain null with a reason. Activity Log generally records management changes, not Key Vault secret reads.
limitations: Resource change history has finite retention and not every resource property is captured.
Activity Log lacks a complete before and after resource payload and does not establish data plane access.

sources.title: ARG property changes and change actor

title: Data collection rules audit
description: Use when investigating data collection rules audit. Audit DCR configuration, associations, destination existence and evidence of recent delivery without misclassifying direct ingestion rules.
analysis: Count distinct associated resource IDs and identify zero association rules, but do not call direct Logs Ingestion API rules orphaned solely because they need no DCRA.
List data sources, named destinations, stream routing and transformKql presence. A configured transform is not evidence it ran successfully.
Flag a deleted workspace only on authorized 404 evidence. Inaccessible destinations have null existence and are not confirmed deleted.
No rows in 24 hours is a delivery concern only for sources expected to emit during the window and when DCR attribution is credible. A workspace row can be delivered by another DCR.
Separate broken stream to destination references, idle sources and unavailable telemetry. Never equate sparse logs with a failed rule.
limitations: DCR specific attribution is not available in every destination table.
Zero DCRA count can be legitimate for direct ingestion or workspace transformation rules.

title: Data Platform Review
description: Use when the user asks for a database review, data platform reliability, SQL or PostgreSQL or MySQL or Cosmos DB resilience, database backup and geo replication, or a data tier health check. Reviews the Azure SQL, PostgreSQL and MySQL Flexible Server, and Cosmos DB resources the agent can read for redundancy, backup, high availability, and network posture, scores each finding by severity, and produces a self contained HTML data platform report.

title: Defender and Advisor recommendation triage
description: Use when investigating defender and advisor recommendation triage. Consolidate current Defender and Advisor recommendations into an owner backlog while preserving source severity, overlap, missing coverage and approval requirements.
analysis: Follow the evidence and analysis workflow in references/workflow.md.
limitations: Live customer validation and separately approved tool access are required.

title: Diagnostic settings coverage audit
description: Use when investigating diagnostic settings coverage audit. Measure supported diagnostic log coverage by resource type using available categories and enabled category groups.
analysis: Use only supported and successfully assessed resources in the coverage denominator and report unsupported and inaccessible counts separately.
A resource has complete log coverage only when the union of enabled log categories across settings covers the required available categories. Disabled entries do not count.
Report zero settings, partial categories and destination misconfiguration as separate findings. Preserve destination workspace or storage IDs internally and alias them for customer sharing.
Platform metrics are collected independently of diagnostic settings. Missing settings means absent configured export for those streams, not that platform metrics do not exist.
limitations: Diagnostic category support varies by resource type and changes over time.
A valid destination reference does not prove successful ingestion or sufficient retention.

sources.title: Diagnostic settings, category groups and automatically collected metrics

title: Executive operational report generation (PDF)
description: Use when investigating executive operational report generation (pdf). Build a locally rendered executive PDF from cost, security, availability, compliance and operational hygiene evidence, with explicit coverage and uncertainty.
analysis: Sum actual spend separately by currency and period, calculate percent change only when previous spend is nonzero, rank top five resource or service drivers, and flag daily cost deviations against the previous comparable period with the threshold recorded.

Show score trend only from historical samples; identify new High recommendations by snapshot difference. Resource Health current state is not an availability percentage or evidence of contractual SLA breach.

Compute incident durations from verified impact intervals and rank the top five. Evaluate SLA claims only against approved service terms, exclusions, measurement basis and customer telemetry; otherwise state not assessed.
Compute compliance from latest resource and policy evaluation pairs, distinguish exempt and unknown states, and rank policies by distinct noncompliant resource count.

Join orphan candidates to actual resource costs, resolve suspected stale RBAC against authorized principal evidence, and compute alert noise ratio with its numerator, denominator and coverage. Never count unresolved identities as confirmed stale.
Produce executive summary, metric table, section details and recommendations. A local preview PDF is not a deployed report, approved disclosure or configured monthly schedule.
limitations: Cost data can arrive late and does not establish orphan savings until ownership and ongoing billing are verified.
Score history, customer impact, SLA breach and RBAC deletion evidence are not guaranteed by read access; missing values remain null.

title: Fired alerts summary (last 24h)
description: Use when investigating fired alerts summary (last 24h). Summarize alerts fired within the last approved 24 hours by severity, actual monitor resolution and unresolved age.
analysis: Group unique instances into Sev0 through Sev4 and preserve a separate unknown severity bucket rather than dropping malformed records.

Compute average resolution time only for instances with verified monitor Resolved timestamps after firing and before the assessment cutoff. Show the resolved denominator and exclude unresolved censored instances.
List unresolved alerts with target resource, rule, firing time and age at END, even if a user marked them Closed.
Separate alerts fired before START but still active into an optional backlog section, not the 24 hour firing count.
limitations: Condition history may not expose an exact first firing for every signal type.
An alert workflow state does not establish recovery of the monitored condition.

sources.title: Alert essentials and monitor condition semantics

title: Identify who added a firewall/NSG rule
description: Use when investigating identify who added a firewall/nsg rule. Attribute NSG and Azure Firewall rule changes using management events and actual property diffs, including Firewall Policy rule collection groups.
analysis: Match caller to a successful write using correlation ID, resource ID and timestamp, retaining actor confidence. Failed writes are attempts, not added rules.
Expand securityRules, applicationRuleCollections, networkRuleCollections, natRuleCollections or Firewall Policy rule collection changes according to the actual resource type.
For each changed rule, report old and new source, destination, protocol and ports from diffs or retained snapshots. Current configuration alone does not prove the historical rule contents.
If a parent write changed several rules, list all verified changed paths; if exact additions cannot be resolved, state collection changed with rule name and values null.
Preserve shared Firewall Policy inheritance and approved parent policy references when identifying the controlling rule.
limitations: Activity Log alone generally does not contain a full NSG or firewall rule before and after payload.
Truncated arrays and shared policies outside approved scope leave exact rule changes unassessed.

title: Incident Triage and Root Cause Assist
description: Use when the user reports an incident, an outage, an alert that fired, a resource that is down or degraded, or asks for triage, root cause analysis, or "what changed". Gathers Resource Health, recent Activity Log changes, and the neighbouring resources for the affected resource, builds a timeline, and helps reason to a probable cause and safe mitigations, then produces a self contained HTML incident report.

title: KQL log queries (common patterns)
description: Use when investigating kql log queries (common patterns). Find severity three and higher application error patterns in an approved workspace without inventing a universal log schema.
analysis: Interpret SeverityLevel >= 3 only for the documented Application Insights severity mapping. State the exact table and schema adapter used.
Group by resource, error code and normalized message pattern; missing ErrorCode is empty or unknown, not an invented code. Preserve counts for all patterns and examples for the five largest.
Separate observed row count from sampled represented telemetry count using ItemCount. Do not infer total application errors if sampling coverage is unknown.
Strip credentials, personal data and customer content from sample messages. A query returning zero with confirmed telemetry coverage is different from a missing table or denied workspace.
limitations: Log Analytics tables are not interchangeable; unsupported schemas require a reviewed adapter.
Row caps, sampling and retention can prevent complete counts; absent or denied data is null.

title: Logic Apps code/definition inspection
description: Use when investigating logic apps code/definition inspection. Inspect Consumption and Standard workflow definitions for resilient error paths, parameterization, loop controls and connector lifecycle evidence.
analysis: Build the runAfter graph for each action scope. Check whether a failed or timed out action is handled by a downstream action or enclosing Scope handler before declaring missing error handling.
Inspect HTTP retryPolicy. Missing explicit policy can mean the documented default retry behavior, not no retries; flag explicit None or a business requirement that defaults do not satisfy.
Evaluate loop concurrency against workload ordering and downstream limits. An omitted explicit limit is a review candidate because platform defaults still exist.
Detect hardcoded environment endpoints, resource IDs and configuration values as parameterization candidates, but redact potential secrets and do not quote them in findings.
Only mark deprecated connector versions with exact official lifecycle evidence for that connector and operation. API version age alone is not deprecation.
limitations: Standard local package may not match the currently deployed revision unless provenance is verified.
Structural inspection cannot prove runtime connector availability or end to end recovery.

sources.title: Logic Apps error handling and default retry policies

title: Messaging delivery failure triage
description: Use when investigating messaging delivery failure triage. Diagnose scoped Azure Service Bus queue backlog and delivery failures from metadata, completion telemetry and approved dead letter reason evidence, without receiving or replaying messages.
frequency: During a delivery failure or backlog investigation
analysis: Compute active backlog growth per minute as (end depth minus start depth) times60 divided by the actual observed interval seconds. Queue depth is a stock and cannot be added to completed message flow.
Compare active growth, dead letter count, transfer dead letter count and completion evidence against customer thresholds. An idle queue with no backlog does not require a positive completion count.
Correlate delivery failures with separately observed lock loss, delivery limit, TTL, filtering and forwarding evidence. Counts alone do not identify the reason or prove messages were lost.
Distinguish source transfer dead letter subqueues from destination entity failures. Missing completion data or missing counters prevents a complete local assessment.
Prepare a recovery proposal that addresses idempotency, duplicate processing, ordering, business reconciliation, canary replay, validation and stop conditions. Never purge or replay automatically.
limitations: Queue metadata and platform counters do not prove business processing success, identify every failure reason or reveal message age distribution.
This adapter does not implement Event Hubs consumer lag, Kafka offsets or topic subscription normalization. Replay and message content inspection are outside the default workflow.

title: Observability Coverage Gap
description: Use when the user asks about monitoring coverage, observability gaps, "where are we blind", missing diagnostic settings, resources with no alerts, no action groups, or no Log Analytics. Cross references the resources the agent can read against their diagnostic settings, metric alerts, action groups, and Log Analytics workspaces, flags the wiring that is missing, and produces a self contained HTML coverage gap report.

title: Operations dashboard generation
description: Use when investigating operations dashboard generation. Generate and locally validate Azure dashboard JSON with discovered metric charts, explicit telemetry gaps and a timestamped Service Health tile.
analysis: Include all requested resource families present in the group. Mark absent families Not applicable and missing telemetry Not assessed.
Chart only metric names verified in that resource's definitions; ensure displayed unit, aggregation and time window are appropriate. SQL DTU is not applicable to every purchasing model.
Use a two column 12 unit grid with no overlapping parts and a full width timestamped health tile. Static health text must never be described as a live Service Health integration.
Validate outer ARM JSON and dashboard part structure locally. State generated preview, cloud validation not run, and deployed false until separately approved and verified.
Retain a previous deployed dashboard export and expected resource diff in the approval package; do not replace an existing dashboard automatically.
limitations: Local syntax checks do not validate Azure portal extension rendering or deployment permissions.
Platform guest memory availability varies; a static health tile is only current at collection time.

sources.title: Dashboard JSON structure and metric chart parts

title: Planned maintenance awareness
description: Use when investigating planned maintenance awareness. Identify planned maintenance overlapping the next approved seven day UTC window and the resources potentially affected.
analysis: Include maintenance whose scheduled interval overlaps [START,END), using start < END and end > START. Do not use lastUpdateTime as the scheduled maintenance time.
Distinguish cancelled, completed, rescheduled and active notices and retain the latest official update with provenance.
Report event name, service, region, UTC start and end, and matched resources. Region matching alone is potential impact, not a guarantee of downtime.
Recommend owner review of redundancy and workload windows; creating reminders, rescheduling workloads or sending notifications is outside this read workflow.
limitations: A short announcement lookback can miss old announcements; explicitly disclose history coverage.
Some notices contain narrative rather than structured schedule or resource details; ambiguous times remain null pending owner review.

title: Post-incident review automation
description: Use when investigating post-incident review automation. Assemble a verified incident timeline, change context, telemetry, impact estimate and owned prevention actions.
analysis: Separate impact start, first alert, human detection, response start, mitigation and verified recovery. User Closed state alone is not recovery evidence.
List changes before and during impact, but label causation as hypothesis until supported by the investigation. Include failed rollback or remediation attempts.
Estimate failed requests and affected workload time from actual telemetry, accounting for sampling and gaps. Customer count is null unless an authorized aggregate source establishes it.
Calculate detection and recovery intervals only when their endpoints are known, retaining uncertainty bounds instead of fabricated timestamps.
Create prevention actions with owner alias, due UTC date, expected verification evidence and priority. No tickets are automatically created or assigned.
limitations: Azure control plane telemetry cannot establish every application or customer impact event.
Temporal correlation alone does not identify root cause; response events may require owner records.

title: Recurring Incident Patterns
description: Use when the user asks about recurring incidents, repeat offenders, chronic problems, "what keeps breaking", flaky resources, or wants to find the workloads that generate the most incidents over time. Aggregates fired alerts and resource health degradations by resource over a window, ranks the repeat offenders, and produces a self contained HTML patterns report.

title: Release regression detection
description: Use when investigating release regression detection. Compare approved release cohorts for error and latency regression, preserving sample coverage and uncertainty without automatically promoting or rolling back a release.
frequency: After a release or reported regression
analysis: Require positive request denominators, the approved minimum sample per cohort and a positive baseline latency. Missing or incomparable cohorts are Not assessed.
Compute error rates independently per cohort. Error increase in percentage points is100 times (current rate minus baseline rate), not relative percent growth.
Compute latency increase percent as100 times (current p95 divided by baseline p95 minus1). Compare both values against separately configured customer thresholds.
A threshold breach recommends investigation or a pause for human review. No breach means only no configured regression observed, not approval to promote or proof of release safety.
Preserve cohort selection, observation windows, telemetry coverage and confounders. Temporal association does not establish a deployment as the cause.
limitations: Aggregate counters alone do not establish statistical significance, causal attribution or whether a critical low traffic route regressed.
Sampled percentiles, mismatched request mix and missing version instrumentation can make the comparison invalid. No automatic rollback or promotion is implemented.
