title: Reliability Posture Review
description: Use when the user asks for a reliability review, resilience assessment, high availability check, single points of failure, a Well-Architected reliability review, or "will we survive a zone or region outage". Scans the resources the agent can read for missing availability zones, single instance workloads, retiring Basic tiers, and single region data services, scores each finding by severity, and produces a self contained HTML resilience scorecard.

title: Resource health status summary
description: Use when investigating resource health status summary. Summarize current Resource Health and preserve inventory resources without supported or accessible health evidence.
analysis: Count Available, Degraded, Unavailable and service reported Unknown separately. Missing health records are Not assessed or unsupported, not service reported Unknown.
List every Degraded and Unavailable resource with returned reason, occurrence or report timestamp and collection time. Do not treat reportedTime as outage start if occurrence time is absent.
Preserve a reconciliation total of inventoried, health assessed, unsupported and inaccessible resources.
Recommend service specific owner investigation for degradation and avoid claiming an SLA breach from current health alone.
limitations: Resource Health support is not universal across resource types.
A current status listing cannot calculate outage duration or contractual availability over a month.

title: Resource metrics analysis
description: Use when investigating resource metrics analysis. Analyze supported resource metrics at five minute resolution, using metric definitions and valid capacity denominators.
analysis: For CPU and other percentage metrics, flag samples above 80 percent directly only when the metric is utilization, not free capacity.
For disk IOPS and network rates, divide by verified applicable resource or disk limits after unit normalization; do not compare raw bytes or counts to the number 80.
For available memory, derive used percentage only with a verified total capacity; retain separate unknown memory checks when no guest collection exists.
Show resource specific supported metrics as well as requested CPU, memory, disk and network coverage. Never replace absent datapoints with zero or combine unlike dimensions.
limitations: Guest memory and some disk counters need separate guest instrumentation.
Platform metrics exist without diagnostic export, but retention, dimensions and resource limits vary by metric and service.

title: Rollback command generation for bad changes
description: Use when investigating rollback command generation for bad changes. Build a reviewed local rollback request from authoritative before values with concurrency and recovery checks, never applying a guessed inverse.
analysis: Identify the exact problematic change from old and new evidence; causal suspicion is not sufficient to revert unrelated later configuration.
Only restore verified writable prior values and compare current state to the recorded after state. Concurrent drift, missing ETag support or unknown before values blocks this generic PATCH route.
Validate schema, dependencies, resource locks, policy constraints and downstream effects before presenting the draft. JSON syntax validation alone is not provider validation.
Require explicit approval of payload hash, resource ID, risk, maintenance window, validation checks and recovery plan before any resource mutation.
After a separately approved apply, re-read configuration, verify workload probes and record actual outcome. A generated command is not a successful rollback.
limitations: Not all Azure resource APIs support PATCH, If-Match or reversible updates.
Truncated history, destructive deletions and secret changes cannot be safely undone by a generic inverse command.

sources.title: ARM validation and what-if versus deployment

title: RTO/RPO gap analysis
description: Use when investigating rto/rpo gap analysis. Compare critical workload recovery objectives with backup, replication and demonstrated restore or failover results.
analysis: Require explicit workload objectives in seconds and distinguish region loss, zone loss, corruption and deletion recovery. Resource redundancy is not automatically a workload recovery plan.
Compare scheduled backup interval and latest successful recovery point age with RPO, allowing for failed jobs and application consistency. Policy frequency alone does not prove achieved RPO.
Compare measured replication lag or last synchronized data watermark with RPO for the same failure mode and time. Geo replication enabled without measured lag leaves achieved RPO unknown.

Calculate drill recovery time from impact or declared recovery start to validated workload availability, and data loss from failure timestamp to recovered application watermark. Compare both to RTO and RPO.

Verify failover plan ownership, dependency ordering and drill recency against customer policy. Missing drill evidence means RTO and recovery feasibility are unverified, even with healthy configuration.
Report per resource gaps and aggregate by workload dependency critical path; do not average resource recovery times to claim workload RTO.
limitations: Backup settings and replica presence cannot establish a demonstrated RTO or end to end RPO.
Some services require data plane or owner drill evidence; inaccessible lag or missing drill results remain null.

title: Service Health incidents & resource impact
description: Use when investigating service health incidents & resource impact. Correlate active Service Health incidents with approved resources, their Resource Health and documented workload dependencies.
analysis: A service and region match establishes potential exposure, not proof of outage. Mark confirmed impact only with event resource evidence, degraded Resource Health or workload telemetry.
Report incident title, services, impacted regions and active or resolved status at the collection instant. Retain events spanning the requested window rather than only events created within it.
Propagate potential impact through explicit dependency edges and show the edge source. Do not infer dependent workloads from matching names alone.
Quote or summarize official mitigation with its update timestamp. Treat proposed architecture alternatives as recommendations requiring separate design and approval.
limitations: Subscription Service Health access does not guarantee resource specific impact detail for every service.
Unsupported or inaccessible Resource Health is null, not Available.

title: SKU reliability assessment
description: Use when investigating sku reliability assessment. Compare production availability requirements with service specific architecture and current SLA evidence, not simplistic SKU labels.
analysis: For VMs distinguish a single zonal instance from multiple instances spread across zones or fault domains. VMSS membership alone does not prove zone resilience or a 99.99 percent commitment.
For SQL compare actual zone redundancy, service tier and regional support with the applicable current SLA clause. A tier label alone is insufficient.
For Storage separate durability, regional recovery and read or write availability. GRS is asynchronous geographic redundancy, not automatically zone redundancy or a universal higher availability SLA.
For App Service evaluate actual plan, instance count, zone redundancy, ASE configuration and dependencies. Premium or ASE alone is not proof the target is met.
Compare numeric commitment to customer target only with exact verified official terms and supported configuration. Otherwise produce architecture concerns with sla_percent null.
Do not multiply or average service SLAs into a workload promise without an explicit dependency and failure model.
limitations: SLA terms depend on configuration, operations, exclusions and the current contract; this library does not embed universal SKU percentages.
Redundancy and durability do not demonstrate workload availability or achieved service level.

title: SLO and error budget analysis
description: Use when investigating slo and error budget analysis. Measure an approved event based service level objective and remaining error budget from scoped application request evidence, without treating missing telemetry as successful requests.
analysis: Require a positive eligible event denominator, classified success evidence, explicit UTC window and customer target. Zero traffic and unknown success values are Not assessed.

Calculate SLI = good_events / total_events. Bad events = total_events minus good_events. Allowed bad events = total_events times (1 minus target). Retain fractional allowance and negative remaining budget rather than rounding away a breach.

Calculate remaining budget = allowed bad events minus bad events, and consumed ratio = bad events / allowed bad events. Compare the event based SLI with the approved target. Do not call this elapsed downtime or a contractual SLA result.
Any incomplete collection prevents Complete even when the observed subset meets the target. Do not claim a short window burn rate without separate windows and denominators.
Recommendations to freeze releases, change alerts or adjust an SLO are drafts. No release system, monitor or target is changed.
limitations: Telemetry sampling weights are estimates of represented events and do not prove full traffic capture. Ingestion delay, workspace scope and instrumentation gaps must be assessed.
A request success field is a technical indicator, not necessarily a successful business transaction. Eligibility, exclusions and the target require customer agreement.

sources.title: AppRequests schema and ItemCount sampling weight

title: Support ticket creation (pre-populated)
description: Use when investigating support ticket creation (pre-populated). Prepare a complete unsent support request and sanitized evidence manifest using current support categories and verified resource telemetry.
analysis: Describe observed symptoms, business impact, UTC timeline and attempted mitigations separately from suspected cause.
Include resource SKU and config summary, supported metrics, error counts, changes and current health with collection timestamps and section coverage.
Select service and problem classification from current catalog results, and validate severity against impact and support plan response obligations without promising response times.
Scan description and evidence for secrets, personal data and unsafe log content. Contact details stay in a private unsent body, not the customer shareable evidence summary.
Require approval of exact payload, contact consent and destination before submission. No ticket number exists until a separately authorized response confirms creation.
limitations: Technical support creation depends on the customer's eligible support plan and permissions.
The support API does not provide a generic evidence attachment or diagnostic sharing consent workflow; review current schema and portal process.

sources.title: Support ticket request fields and prerequisites

title: VM performance anomaly detection
description: Use when investigating vm performance anomaly detection. Compare production VM performance with the same UTC quarter hour on seven preceding days, preserving missing guest metric coverage.
analysis: For each VM, metric, dimension and instance, select the seven preceding daily samples with the same UTC quarter hour as the current completed interval. Exclude current values from baseline.
Calculate sample mean and sample standard deviation. Flag current > mean + 2*stdev for CPU, used memory, disk queue and network; for free memory flag current < mean - 2*stdev.
Require at least five valid matched historical intervals and adequate within interval sample coverage; otherwise baseline and anomaly verdict are null. Record the minimum sample rule.
For zero standard deviation, report changed from constant baseline without dividing by zero. Network totals and rates must use consistent interval units.
Correlate anomalies with VM power state and approved changes; statistical deviation is not proof of customer impact.
limitations: Memory and disk queue guest counters are not guaranteed platform metrics.
Seven daily comparable windows offer a limited baseline and do not model weekly seasonality.

title: Well-Architected Review
description: Use when the user asks for a Well-Architected review, a WAF assessment, a Well-Architected Framework scorecard, a pillar review, or "how well architected are we". Runs a curated set of high signal checks across all five Well-Architected pillars (Reliability, Security, Cost Optimization, Operational Excellence, Performance Efficiency), scores each pillar, and produces a single self contained HTML scorecard.

title: Workbook auto-generation
description: Use when investigating workbook auto-generation. Produce an ARM workbook draft with workload specific health, metric, error, cost and change panels from collected evidence, clearly labeled as a snapshot preview.
analysis: Detect workload resource types before selecting metric panels and preserve every requested section, marking unavailable data explicitly.
Health is a collection time snapshot; metric and error trend rows have explicit UTC bins; cost has explicit currency and dates; changes include actor aliases.
Keep serializedData a JSON string containing Notebook/1.0 and valid typed items. No secrets, raw credentials or password workbook parameters are allowed.
Validate both ARM and inner workbook JSON locally, verify all five sections and source IDs, and record preview versus deployed state separately.
Do not promise live refresh for snapshot panels. Cloud rendering, template what-if, publishing and scheduling are distinct approval steps with previous version backup and rollback.
limitations: The baseline generated workbook contains real evidence snapshots, not live refresh panels.
Local JSON validation cannot prove portal rendering, current cost completeness or query permission in another identity.

title: Workload context and Azure consultation
description: Use when investigating workload context and azure consultation. Ground Azure guidance in the approved workload inventory, objectives and current Microsoft guidance, separating facts from hypotheses and proposed changes.
frequency: When a workload team needs contextual Azure guidance
analysis: Follow the evidence and analysis workflow in references/workflow.md.
limitations: Live customer validation and separately approved tool access are required.

title: Azure Firewall rule generation
description: Use when investigating azure firewall rule generation. Create a narrowly scoped local Azure Firewall network rule proposal with reviewed CLI text and Bicep, never deploy it during assessment.
analysis: Validate source CIDR against the observed subnet, destination against the owner approved target and ports/protocol against the application requirement. Reject wildcard destinations, broad source networks and unresolved placeholders.

Determine classic versus policy management and inspect inherited policy/rule collections, DNAT precedence, overlapping allows/denies and occupied priorities. A new allow cannot override an earlier matching deny.
Confirm the source route traverses this firewall and return traffic has a viable route. A rule proposal does not establish that traffic will reach the firewall.

Generate the local collection for the exact approved TCP or UDP flow using literal IP/CIDR or FQDN fields as appropriate. FQDN network rules require verified DNS proxy and no wildcard; prefer an application rule for HTTP/S or MSSQL when its protocol semantics are required.
Preserve all existing rule collections when integrating Bicep. The fragment is not a complete firewall resource and must never replace the current rule array unreviewed.

Require local Bicep compile, reviewed deployment diff, owner approval, bounded positive and negative flow tests, monitoring and rollback to the recorded prior rule configuration before any separately authorized deployment.
limitations: The local draft supports TCP/UDP network rules and same subscription policy targets. Cross subscription policy scope, ICMP and application rules require a separately reviewed adaptation.
Firewall configuration, routing, DNS proxy and precedence must be validated together; generating a rule is not proof of allowed connectivity.

title: DDoS protection coverage audit
description: Use when investigating ddos protection coverage audit. Assess DDoS Network and IP Protection coverage for public facing VNet resources and provide cost estimates only from approved rate evidence.
analysis: Build public facing resource counts per VNet by resolving public frontend and NIC subnet references, including Application Gateway. Count distinct public owners and PIPs separately.

Evaluate VNet Network Protection enabled plus a valid associated plan, and evaluate explicit public IP protection mode independently. IP Protection can cover an individual eligible PIP without a VNet Network Protection plan.

Flag public facing resources without demonstrated enhanced protection as customer policy review findings, while distinguishing platform infrastructure protection from Network/IP Protection. Unsupported resource/PIP SKUs require documented eligibility checks.
Do not automatically flag an entire VNet as uncovered when all eligible public IPs have IP Protection. Show per PIP coverage, VNet plan coverage and mixed coverage separately.

Estimate plan or IP Protection incremental monthly cost only from rate_evidence, considering already paid shared plans, included quantities and overages. Do not multiply a shared plan base price by every VNet.

When rates or allocation are unknown output estimate null and request a rate verification. Recommendations must consider security benefits and existing shared coverage rather than claim guaranteed savings.
limitations: Public endpoint eligibility and DDoS feature scope differ by resource and public IP SKU; configuration must not be generalized across every PaaS endpoint.
A shared plan has included quantities and allocation constraints, so missing rate evidence prevents a reliable incremental cost estimate.

title: DNS/VPN troubleshooting
description: Use when investigating dns/vpn troubleshooting. Correlate observed DNS response failures with VPN connection, tunnel and BGP evidence while preserving unknown historical connection times.
analysis: Group NXDOMAIN and SERVFAIL independently by client, domain and query type. NXDOMAIN can be intentional, while SERVFAIL indicates resolver processing failure; neither alone proves the VPN caused the response.
Identify disconnected/unknown VPN connections, distinguish provisioning failures and current tunnel state, and join each to gateway ID and peer endpoint.
For BGP enabled connections flag peers not in their documented healthy state. For static routing connections mark BGP Not applicable rather than failed.

From retained diagnostics extract last successful connection event and explicit disconnect reason only when the log format supports them. Current Connected state is not a historical last successful connection timestamp.
Correlate DNS failure spikes and tunnel/BGP events by time and client network. Distinguish evidence of temporal association from a proven route or resolver cause.

Recommend ordered checks: private DNS zone/link and forwarding path, expected DNS records, effective routes, on premises DNS reachability, tunnel parameters and BGP routes. No gateway reset, DNS change or packet capture is executed.
limitations: DNS evidence is limited to configured Azure Firewall DNS proxy logs and does not cover every resolver.
Gateway APIs may not expose disconnect reasons or historical connect times; absent diagnostics leave those fields null.

title: DNS zone record hygiene
description: Use when investigating dns zone record hygiene. Assess public and private A, AAAA and CNAME records with scoped resource ownership and resolver evidence while avoiding false dangling DNS claims.
analysis: Normalize DNS names and IP literals, preserving zone ID, family, record type and TTL. Parse A/AAAA with an IP library and compare exact IPs to the complete approved ownership map.

An IP not in current approved Azure inventory is unmatched, not necessarily dangling: check external_target_allowlist, on premises ownership, other approved subscriptions and service managed endpoints before raising a deletion candidate.

Resolve CNAME chains through the approved resolver, detect loops and bound chain depth. A response from the wrong DNS vantage does not establish private record failure; record timeout/refused/SERVFAIL separately from NXDOMAIN.
For alias targetResource IDs use an authorized resource read. Repeatable 404 can establish a missing target candidate, while 403 and unapproved cross subscription targets remain unknown.
Azure alias records can become empty record sets when a supported target is deleted; report empty alias sets separately instead of assuming a stale nonempty target pointer always remains.
Recommend owner verification and TTL aware change planning. Never delete records, mutate aliases or treat one transient resolution failure as proof of a takeover vulnerability.
limitations: Approved subscription IP inventory cannot prove global ownership or absence of on premises/external targets.
Private DNS resolution depends on the network vantage, forwarding and links, and transient resolver errors are not deleted resource evidence.

title: ExpressRoute / VPN Gateway health
description: Use when investigating expressroute / vpn gateway health. Assess circuit, peering, tunnel and BGP health with one hour throughput evidence and explicit capacity assumptions.
analysis: Reconcile every approved circuit and gateway inventory item with an assessed family. Classic resources use the supplied status reads; Virtual WAN or unsupported child inventory requires provider specific details and is Not assessed until supplied, never healthy by omission.

Flag provisioning failures, unprovisioned provider circuits, disconnected VPN tunnels and unhealthy observed BGP peers. Distinguish maintenance windows, static routing and missing diagnostic permission.

For ExpressRoute combine peering configuration with BGP/ARP availability metric evidence where supported. A peering enabled flag is not established BGP, and an unavailable metric leaves session health unknown.

Calculate ingress and egress separately over the last hour, normalizing units. Compare per direction rates to circuit provider bandwidth where documented, not a sum of both directions against a single direction limit.

For gateway throughput use only a documented relevant SKU capacity with connection/instance scope. Rated throughput is not a guaranteed workload limit; if capacity is unknown utilization percent is null.
Report current status, last samples, coverage, observed peak and average, capacity source and candidate owner checks. Never reset gateways, change peerings or submit quota requests.
limitations: Provisioning success and peering Enabled do not prove end to end connectivity or established BGP.
Gateway capacity depends on SKU and workload, and Virtual WAN status interfaces differ from classic virtual network gateways.

sources.title: ExpressRoute monitoring and required diagnostic routing

title: Firewall log analysis (KQL)
description: Use when investigating firewall log analysis (kql). Analyze denied flows, internal source denials, approved suspicious destination indicators and rule collection activity with honest byte volume limits.
analysis: Rank denied network tuples by log hit count, preserving source, destination, port and protocol. Denial counts are not unique connections and must not be labeled as such.
Analyze all internal source denials against customer CIDRs, not just RFC1918 or the overall top twenty. Correlate approved application flows before suggesting a misconfiguration.
Join allowed IP/FQDN hits to approved indicators with source timestamp and expiration. Report false positive review and do not infer suspiciousness from an arbitrary destination list.

Report hourly hit counts per rule collection, action and table. Per collection traffic bytes remain null because these tables do not contain payload byte counts; present aggregate DataProcessed separately.

Verify log category coverage, table plan, diagnostic destination, observation bounds and partial query warnings. If legacy mode is configured, report that the supplied resource specific queries cannot assess those records until a separately verified legacy parser is supplied.
Recommend narrowly scoped rule or application owner review, never automatically add allow rules, block indicators or change diagnostic routing.
limitations: Resource specific rule logs report rule hits rather than complete flow payload volume; per collection network bytes cannot be derived from _BilledSize.
Logging mode, table plan and retention can limit coverage; an empty or missing table is not evidence of no traffic.

title: Flow Log Firewall Advisor
description: Use when the user asks what firewall rules a virtual network needs, wants to move a VNet behind Azure Firewall, asks what traffic to allow, mentions deriving rules from flow logs, asks about egress from a VNet, lateral movement between subnets, or wants to know what is actually talking to what. Reads VNet flow logs through Traffic Analytics, reconstructs the connections that really occurred, and produces a severity ranked review report with proposed Azure Firewall network rules and the evidence behind each one.

title: Network Exposure Review
description: Use when the user asks about internet exposure, public exposure, attack surface, open ports, NSG rules open to the internet, public IPs, storage public access, or PaaS resources reachable from the internet. Scans the resources the agent can read for network security group rules open to the internet, storage and PaaS with public access, scores each by severity, and produces a self contained HTML exposure report.

title: Network topology diagram
description: Use when investigating network topology diagram. Generate a local evidence backed Mermaid topology draft containing VNets, subnets, directed peering states, gateways, private endpoints and subnet resource placement.
analysis: Reconcile the diagram node set to approved VNet and resource inventories and record page completeness. Include every subnet and its observed prefix; unknown prefixes are labeled rather than guessed.
Render each peering as a directed relationship with its own peeringState. Connected on one side does not establish healthy bidirectional connectivity.

Place gateways, private endpoints and NIC based resources only from explicit subnet references. Join VM to NIC references, gateway connection peer references and private link target IDs; do not infer placement from names.
Show VPN/ExpressRoute gateways and related circuits even if they have no direct subnet field. Label configuration relationships rather than imply live traffic reachability.

Validate Mermaid parse and locally render for visual inspection, checking counts, missing nodes, edge direction and clipped labels. Include UTC evidence timestamp and gaps in the report accompanying the diagram.
Treat addresses, names and topology as sensitive customer metadata. Generate a local draft only and obtain destination approval plus any requested redaction before distribution.
limitations: Configuration topology does not prove effective routes, firewall reachability or application connectivity.
Cross subscription references and Resource Graph child omissions may leave incomplete external nodes; no live status is invented.

title: Overly permissive NSG rules audit
description: Use when investigating overly permissive nsg rules audit. Identify broadly allowing NSG rules with correct priority, direction, augmented ranges and association context.
analysis: Evaluate Allow rules first, separating custom from default and inbound from outbound. Broad Deny rules are not permissive allow findings.

Normalize sourceAddressPrefix/sourceAddressPrefixes and destination equivalents. Flag *, Any if returned, 0.0.0.0/0 and ::/0; retain Internet and other service tags as distinct semantics rather than expanding them from memory.

Normalize destinationPortRange/destinationPortRanges, parse valid inclusive intervals and compute union cardinality to avoid counting overlaps twice. Flag wildcard ports and ranges spanning more than 100 distinct ports.

Apply rules in increasing numeric priority within each direction. Identify potentially shadowed broad rules and preserve uncertainty where ASGs, service tags or multiple target scopes prevent exact local evaluation.

Do not exempt broad sources just because ports look like load balancer ports. Only a documented source/service/protocol/purpose match, such as a legitimate AzureLoadBalancer probe rule, can satisfy an approved exception.

Report NIC/subnet associations, full source/destination/protocol/ports and the exact triggering condition. Recommend least scope changes for owner review without claiming effective reachability from rule text alone.
limitations: NSG rules alone do not prove public reachability because routing, public IP translation, other NSGs and guest controls also apply.
Service tags and ASGs require additional membership context for exact shadow or reachability evaluation.

title: Private endpoint & public exposure audit
description: Use when investigating private endpoint & public exposure audit. Assess PaaS public network configuration and approved private endpoint coverage without equating endpoint existence with public access being disabled.
analysis: Normalize public access into enabled, disabled or unknown using documented semantics for each service; do not infer enabled or disabled solely from a missing publicNetworkAccess field.

Join endpoint connections by target ARM ID and requested subresource. Only Approved connections count as usable private endpoint configuration; Pending, Rejected and Disconnected are separate findings.
Flag public access enabled with no approved private endpoint as the requested review pattern, while separately flagging policy requiring private only even when both public and private access coexist.

Evaluate service firewall/default action and IP/VNet/access restriction exceptions before claiming internet reachability. PublicNetworkAccess enabled with default deny is not equivalent to open to every source.

Report only FQDN/IP values actually exposed by resource metadata, such as Storage primaryEndpoints, SQL fullyQualifiedDomainName, Key Vault vaultUri, Cosmos documentEndpoint and App Service defaultHostName. Never fabricate a hostname from a resource name.
Separate configuration posture from effective DNS and route reachability; approved private endpoint configuration still needs DNS and client path validation.
limitations: An enabled public endpoint is not proof of unrestricted internet reachability, and an approved private endpoint does not automatically disable public access.
Service defaults, child access restrictions and endpoints in other subscriptions require explicit evidence; unknown reads are not absence.

sources.title: Private endpoint approval, subresources and service coverage

title: Public IP inventory & justification
description: Use when investigating public ip inventory & justification. Inventory public IP ownership and flag unattached, stopped VM and nonproduction use for owner justification without assuming the IP is unnecessary.
analysis: Resolve each public IP through all returned association types. Mark unattached only when no owner references remain and the relevant owner inventory is complete.
For directly VM owned IP configurations, flag stopped and deallocated states separately. A retained static address may be intentional, and stopped VM state is not a deletion recommendation.
Classify production/nonproduction using customer rules and report the evidence source. Unknown environment remains unknown; nonproduction public exposure is a review flag, not inherently forbidden.
Preserve SKU, allocation method, IP value and owner ID/type. A null dynamic address is unallocated, not an invalid resource.

Keep creation date null if not supplied by trustworthy provider metadata or archived creation records. Request an owner justification and identify DNS/allowlist dependencies before recommending address release.
limitations: Static addresses may be retained for DNS, partner allowlists or recovery even when a VM is stopped.
Not every public IP owner or creation timestamp is visible from a single resource API.

sources.title: Public IP translation and effective network path context

title: SSL/TLS certificate expiration tracking
description: Use when investigating ssl/tls certificate expiration tracking. Track certificate expiry across Key Vault, App Service, Application Gateway, Front Door and API Management without retrieving private keys or assuming automatic renewal succeeded.
analysis: Inventory and report coverage for all five families, separating stored certificates, installed certificates and active listener/domain bindings.

Resolve each binding to its exact certificate thumbprint or version. A versionless vault reference may auto rotate, but verify actual deployment metadata and do not infer rotation succeeded from a newer stored version.
Use public certificate parsing or authoritative returned expirationDate/attributes metadata. Do not substitute certificate policy issuer provider name for the actual X509 issuer.

Compute fractional days remaining from expiry UTC minus assessment_utc. Classify expired below zero, expiring within 30 days inclusive, and later otherwise. A null expiry is Not assessed, not healthy.

For Front Door managed/classic certificates with no exposed expiry record platform renewal ownership and deployment state but retain expiry null. Do not equate provisioning success with a fresh served certificate.

Deduplicate certificate versions by thumbprint for inventory counts while retaining all affected bindings. Recommend owner renewal and post renewal binding verification, with no secret access or live endpoint probes in this read workflow.
limitations: Some managed Front Door or secret only certificates do not expose expiry/public DER through these metadata APIs; unknown fields stay null.
Stored certificate expiry does not prove which certificate is currently served on every endpoint, and automatic renewal must not be assumed successful.

title: VNet peering health check
description: Use when investigating vnet peering health check. Assess both directed peering objects, address overlap and valid complementary gateway transit settings rather than requiring incorrect symmetry.
analysis: For every directed peering find a reciprocal object whose remoteVirtualNetwork.id equals the local VNet ID. Record local and remote states independently and flag non Connected states.
Missing reciprocal objects are findings only after a complete authorized remote list. An unreadable remote scope is Not assessed, not missing.
Parse all local and remote IPv4/IPv6 CIDRs with an IP network library and test same family interval overlap. Validate current versus cached remote address space and report stale sync metadata.

Gateway transit is intentionally complementary, not symmetric: if one side useRemoteGateways is true, the remote side must allowGatewayTransit and own a compatible gateway; the consuming VNet must not have its own conflicting gateway.
Both sides useRemoteGateways, missing gateway owner, or multiple remote gateway choices are review findings. Both transit flags false can be healthy when transit is not required.
Report allowVirtualNetworkAccess and allowForwardedTraffic by direction plus design intent. A Connected control plane state does not certify end to end routes or application traffic.
limitations: Cross tenant or unapproved remote subscriptions can prevent reciprocal validation without proving a broken peering.
Connected state and complementary transit flags do not validate route tables, NSGs or on premises connectivity.

title: CI/CD pipeline failure investigation
description: Use when investigating ci/cd pipeline failure investigation. Inspect an approved build timeline and bounded task logs to identify the first evidenced failure, distinguish downstream symptoms and draft a safe fix proposal.
analysis: Follow the evidence and analysis workflow in references/workflow.md.
limitations: Live customer validation and separately approved tool access are required.

title: Export existing resources to ARM/Bicep
description: Use when investigating export existing resources to arm/bicep. Export only approved resources into private local ARM or Bicep drafts, parameterize reviewed values, redact secrets and validate without deploying.
analysis: Treat export as a starting snapshot, not a proven redeployable backup. Record every export warning, unsupported type and omitted resource and compare selected inventory with exported resources.

Review the documented resource group export count limit and split by supported selections where appropriate. Azure Data Factory needs its dedicated export process; do not claim generic ARM export covers it.

Parameterize actual names, SKU choices and locations with nonsecret current values in the parameter file. Redact secret values in both parameters and nested resource properties before generating shareable drafts.
Remove read only and generated properties by resource type schema, not a global deletion of all IDs. Preserve writable dependency references and explicitly repair missing dependencies.

For Bicep, decompile locally, organize reviewed modules by resource family and validate their interfaces and dependencies through local build. Compilation is not a deployment or service behavior test.

Report artifact state Draft, local validation result, cloud validation Not run and deployed false. Include exact approved scope, expected resource diff, previous configuration evidence and redeployment recovery plan before requesting apply approval.
limitations: Export schemas can be incomplete or stale, password parameters may be omitted and some resource types need dedicated manual export routes.
Local JSON parsing and Bicep build do not establish safe redeployment, dependency completeness or secret free output without manual review.

sources.title: CLI export, resource selection, parameter defaults and limits

title: Failed deployments in last 24h
description: Use when investigating failed deployments in last 24h. Find failed ARM deployments and operation errors at approved subscription, resource group and optional management group scopes.
analysis: Report deployment ID, scope, resource group where applicable, name, timestamp, top level error code, sanitized message and correlation ID.
Expand nested error details into actionable root cause codes rather than grouping every failure solely under DeploymentFailed.
Group by stable error code and distinguish policy denial, quota, permissions and template validation evidence without guessing missing causes.
Deduplicate nested and parent deployments when counting incident groups while preserving each failed deployment record.
History that was deleted, aged out or denied remains a coverage gap. No failures in incomplete history is not a complete clean result.
limitations: Deployment history has retention and deletion limits; it is not a complete permanent audit trail.
Error messages can contain sensitive request data and require redaction.

title: Pre-Change Readiness
description: Use before a launch, a migration, a deployment, or a big change, or when the user asks for a readiness check, a go or no-go, or "are we ready to ship". Runs reliability, internet exposure, and capacity checks scoped to one target subscription or resource group and returns a go, caution, or no-go verdict per category, as a self contained HTML readiness report.

title: Standard platform request planning
description: Use when investigating standard platform request planning. Validate a platform request against approved policies and conventions, draft the smallest change and rollback plan, and prepare repository and documentation updates for review.
frequency: When a standard platform request is raised
analysis: Follow the evidence and analysis workflow in references/workflow.md.
limitations: Live customer validation and separately approved tool access are required.

title: AI model inventory & retirement lifecycle
description: Use when investigating ai model inventory & retirement lifecycle. Inventory Azure OpenAI and Foundry model deployments and classify lifecycle only against an explicitly dated official model and version schedule.
analysis: Build one record per deployment, including subscription, group, parent account/workspace, deployment name, model name/version, hosting offering, region and creation date if supplied. Do not infer deployment date from an account's creation time.

Refresh and archive the official retirement schedule during execution. Match exact model and version plus documented deployment type/region exceptions; never use name only or invent a replacement for an empty schedule cell.

Classify Retired when a confirmed retirement date is before assessment_utc, Retiring soon for dates from assessment through 90 days, and Current for confirmed later dates or explicitly confirmed no announced retirement in the applicable schedule.
Unmatched offerings, unresolved versions and unavailable schedules are Not assessed, not Current. Third party and self hosted models require their own authoritative lifecycle source.

Compute days_until_retirement from UTC dates, retaining negative values for retired versions. Recommend only the replacement stated in the source, otherwise null, and require compatibility, availability and quota testing before migration.
Summarize total deployment counts by lifecycle including unknown, alongside coverage per provider and offering. The catalog source date is not a promise that the schedule will remain current.
limitations: Foundry offerings do not all expose identical ARM metadata or use the OpenAI retirement schedule.
Retirement dates, replacements and regional exceptions change; rerun official source verification at assessment time.

title: Azure Architecture Skill
description:
Build a first-pass Azure landing-zone architecture and cost estimate from a VM inventory workbook.
Use this skill when the user wants a draw.io architecture, Azure stencil diagram, landing-zone recommendation,
migration target design, or rough-order monthly Azure cost estimate for a server estate.
Outputs typically include a draw.io document, an Excel cost workbook, a CSV summary, and JSON metadata.

title: Deprecation and Retirement Tracker
description: Use when the user asks about deprecations, retirements, end of life runtimes or platforms, unsupported versions, retiring SKUs, old Kubernetes or AKS versions, legacy or classic resources, or upcoming forced migrations. Scans the resources the agent can read for end of life runtimes, retired service tiers, classic resources, and old platform versions, and produces a self contained HTML deprecation report.

title: Extension health across VMs
description: Use when investigating extension health across vms. Assess VM extension provisioning and runtime health with evidence for prolonged transitions and documented extension conflicts.
analysis: Flag model provisioningState Failed and runtime handler/substatus error levels separately. A succeeded model does not override a current handler error.

For Transitioning, establish duration only using a provider status timestamp with known meaning or observations of the same uninterrupted transition at least one hour apart. A single snapshot cannot establish duration.
Where two snapshots are used, report a lower bound of observed transition duration and possible unobserved state changes rather than assert continuous failure without evidence.
Check publisher/type/version pairs against the reviewed incompatibility matrix. Without a documented pair report conflict assessment unknown, not a guessed conflict.
Correlate agent readiness and VM power state, identify affected VM and extension, and recommend a specific vendor troubleshooting check. Do not uninstall, reapply, restart or execute guest scripts.
limitations: Status timestamps and transitioning duration are not uniformly supplied, so a point in time snapshot cannot prove a one hour transition.
Guest output can include sensitive content and stopped VMs can expose stale instance views.

title: Management Group hierarchy audit
description: Use when investigating management group hierarchy audit. Audit an approved management group subtree, its direct and inherited policy/RBAC assignments, empty nodes and root subscriptions without inventing policy conflicts.
analysis: Build the hierarchy adjacency tree and count both direct child subscriptions and all descendant subscriptions per group, clearly labeling the two counts.
Flag groups with no visible child groups or subscriptions only when the group read is complete. A subtree root is not necessarily the tenant root.
Flag subscriptions directly beneath the actual tenant root only when root identity and membership are in approved evidence; otherwise mark the root placement check Not assessed.
List direct and inherited policies and role assignments per node, preserving scope and condition. Exemptions and notScopes can change applicability.

For potential policy conflicts resolve definitions, initiative references, parameter values, aliases, applicable resource conditions, effects and enforcement modes. Prove incompatible constraints on the same applicable resource set, such as disjoint allowed location sets, before asserting conflict.

Different policy names or a child audit alongside a parent deny are not automatically conflicts. Unsupported policy semantics yield a review candidate with the exact unresolved expression, not a definitive conclusion.
limitations: Reader visibility can be partial and cannot prove tenant wide emptiness or completeness.
General Azure Policy conflict determination requires expression and parameter evaluation; text differences alone are not conflicts.

title: Move resources between subscriptions
description: Use when investigating move resources between subscriptions. Produce a local cross subscription move feasibility and validation plan without executing a move or relying on a nonexistent validate only CLI switch.
analysis: Verify both subscriptions are active and in the same tenant. Confirm each top level type supports the requested cross subscription move using current official move support and service specific guidance; reject unknown support.

Build dependency closure from provider references, including shared networking, disks and nested resources. Exclude child resources from the explicit top level move list where they move with parents. Unknown dependencies block a Ready recommendation.

Evaluate inherited/direct locks, provider registration and target service quotas for all regions and families. ReadOnly locks are a documented blocker; other lock effects require authoritative validation rather than blanket claims.

Compare target inherited policy effects, required tags and deny conditions, resource ID changes, source scoped role assignments and target inherited access. Role assignments do not simply transfer with moved resource IDs.

Generate only the local draft containing exact source, target, selected resources, validation request and never executed move arguments. Validation is a separate privileged action and the read workflow must not call it.

Require explicit approval for validation, capture asynchronous validation status and errors, then obtain distinct move approval with downtime/management lock impact, backups, dependency checks, owner acceptance, post move tests and a feasible rollback or restoration plan. Validation success is not a completed move.
limitations: Move support and dependency requirements are resource type specific; a generic inventory cannot certify every service move.
Server validation requires separately approved action permissions and may be asynchronous; this read assessment intentionally does not execute it.

sources.title: Move checklist, changed IDs and validateMoveResources

title: Quota and Limit Watch
description: Use when the user asks about quotas, service limits, capacity headroom, vCPU or core limits, public IP or network limits, "will a deployment or scale out fail", or approaching Azure limits. Reads Azure usage and quota counters for compute, network, and storage across the regions the agent's resources sit in, flags any counter close to its limit, and produces a self contained HTML quota headroom report.

title: Resource age tracking
description: Use when investigating resource age tracking. Find older resources with no observed management writes in the available 90 day window and attach cost for owner review, not an unused resource verdict.
analysis: Subtract age_months calendar months from end_utc with a documented month end rule, rather than approximating months as a fixed number of days.
Identify resources with known creation time before the cutoff. Unknown creation timestamps stay Not assessed for age regardless of resource name or first observed event.

Find successful /write operations for each normalized resource ID and report the latest observed management event separately from latest write. If none exist, latest_write is null with no write observed in the covered interval.
Flag old resources with no observed writes as decommission review candidates only when coverage is adequate. Explicitly state that stable resources can be heavily used on the data plane.

Join last complete monthly costs and currency, retaining unattributed cost as null. Owner review must include utilization, dependencies, recovery needs and business value before any retirement decision.
limitations: No writes in Activity Log does not mean no reads, no data plane use or no business value.
Native retention and provider timestamp gaps prevent lifetime activity reconstruction.

title: Resource group sprawl detection
description: Use when investigating resource group sprawl detection. Assess empty, single resource, temporary naming and missing tag resource groups with observed cost and unknown creation dates preserved.
analysis: Left join all approved resource groups with distinct current resource counts. Zero is valid only after the inventory is complete and authorized.

Flag zero resource groups and single resource groups as organizational review candidates, not automatically removable or mergeable; resource groups can be deliberate lifecycle, permission or deployment boundaries.
Apply customer approved temporary/test naming patterns only within documented production scope. Naming is a heuristic and must not override tags or owner confirmation.
Evaluate required tag presence, empty values and allowed values, preserving exemptions. Do not invent required tags from common conventions.
Attach monthly cost by group/currency and creation date only if proven. Recommend owner actions including retain, investigate or consolidation review, never execute a move or deletion.
limitations: Empty resource groups can be intentional boundaries, and current resource count does not eliminate historical charges.
Group creation timestamps are not uniformly available and naming alone cannot establish environment or ownership.

sources.title: Resource group dependency and move considerations

title: Resource lock compliance audit
description: Use when investigating resource lock compliance audit. Assess effective inherited management lock coverage for production VMs, SQL servers, storage accounts, Key Vaults and AKS.
analysis: Select the requested five resource families only in subscriptions whose documented Environment tag qualifies as Production. Explicitly report unsupported or missing subscription tag visibility.
For each resource evaluate subscription, group and resource locks along its actual scope ancestry. ReadOnly is stronger than CanNotDelete and inherited coverage counts.
Flag targets lacking an effective CanNotDelete or ReadOnly lock unless an approved exemption applies. Retain exemption rationale and scope.
Recommend CanNotDelete for deletion protection when aligned with customer policy; recommend ReadOnly only after checking blocked operational POST actions, service management and automation impact.
Explain that locks protect control plane operations, not SQL rows, storage objects or Key Vault data. Effective lock coverage is not a backup or data protection verdict.
limitations: An empty direct lock list does not rule out inherited protection.
ReadOnly can block required management operations, and neither lock type protects underlying data plane content.

title: Resources created yesterday
description: Use when investigating resources created yesterday. Identify resources with evidence of creation in the last 24 hours, attribute the creator where possible and assess naming without mistaking updates for creates.
analysis: Select resources with a trustworthy createdTime or systemData.createdAt inside [start_utc,end_utc). If only a write exists, label creation candidate unless a Created result and supporting provider evidence establish a new resource.
Correlate resource ID, timestamp and correlation ID with successful Activity Log records; report the creator from systemData or event claims with its source. Missing attribution remains null.

Classify ARM deployment only when deployment operation evidence targets the resource. Service principal callers suggest automation but do not prove a pipeline; portal/manual origin remains unknown without client or pipeline evidence.
Apply the type specific approved naming rules, including case and allowed exceptions. Without a supplied rule mark naming Not assessed rather than invent a convention.

Report resource name, type, group, subscription, creation time, creator, deployment evidence, classification and naming finding. Preserve resources created and deleted within the interval as event only candidates rather than current inventory.
limitations: A write event is not sufficient proof of creation, and creation timestamps are not supported uniformly.
Activity Log caller and deployment history rarely prove portal versus pipeline origin without additional evidence.

title: Subscription hygiene score
description: Use when investigating subscription hygiene score. Compute a transparent customer defined hygiene index with six weighted evidence components and explicit unknown coverage.
analysis: Compute component ratios from eligible assessed denominators: compliant tags 20 percent, effective locks 15 percent, required enabled alert coverage 20 percent, qualifying diagnostics 15 percent, policy compliance 15 percent and classic Defender score 15 percent.

For tags, locks, alerts and diagnostics count fully passing resources divided by eligible resources under coverage_policy. Expand alert scope or tag based criteria before counting; diagnostic settings must include required categories and a valid destination.

For policy use compliant divided by compliant plus noncompliant evaluated eligible resources, with exemptions and unknown states separately listed. For Defender use returned current/max only when max is positive and the selected initiative is identified.

Calculate total score = 100 * sum(weight * component_ratio) only when all applicable components are assessed. For unavailable components provide a known contribution lower bound and potential upper bound, but total score null; do not renormalize missing evidence into a pass.

If a component has no eligible resources, require a documented customer policy for not applicable weighting; otherwise keep the aggregate unassessed. This is a customer hygiene index, not an official Azure score.
For complete totals below 70 rank improvements by lost weighted points and action effort. For incomplete totals prioritize evidence gaps before score based conclusions.
limitations: This composite index is not an official Azure compliance or security score and depends on the agreed coverage policy.
The classic Azure secure score differs from the risk based Cloud Secure Score, and diagnostic configuration does not establish successful log delivery.

title: Subscription limits approaching
description: Use when investigating subscription limits approaching. Assess regional vCPU family, public IP, VNet and storage account usage against returned subscription limits.
analysis: Create one record per subscription, region and quota identifier, retaining the returned scope and unit. Avoid double counting total vCPU and family quotas as additive capacity.
Compute utilization = 100 * currentValue / limit for positive limits. Zero, missing or unsupported limits yield utilization null with reason; no divide by zero.
Flag strictly above 80 percent and report remaining headroom and the exact count needed to reach the limit. Exactly 80 percent is watch, not the requested above threshold finding.
Cover vCPU families, public IP categories, VNet counts and storage account counts separately for every approved region; unreadable families/regions are Not assessed.
Recommend capacity planning or a quota request for the specific provider and region. Do not promise approval, physical capacity or SKU availability from quota headroom.
limitations: Quota headroom is not a reservation or guarantee of regional SKU capacity.
Some quota categories differ by SKU or provider and may not be exposed by a single usage API; unavailable categories stay unknown.

title: Certificate renewal automation
description: Use when investigating certificate renewal automation. Inspect certificate expiry and renewal evidence, then prepare a certificate specific renewal or owner notification package without issuing certificates.
analysis: Derive subject and issuer from certificate policy and public certificate metadata, and compute expiry from attributes.expires. Preserve null expiry and do not interpret disabled certificates as safely retired without owner confirmation.
Inspect lifetimeActions for AutoRenew versus EmailContacts and issuer configuration. An AutoRenew entry alone does not prove the CA integration or consumer version rollover works.
Flag certificates with fewer than 30 days remaining without a viable renewal path. Include existing pending operation status and error, or supplied CA failure notices, as renewal failure evidence.

Validate the draft against issuer type and consumer rebinding needs. Require separate approval to create a certificate version, merge a signed certificate, change lifetime policy, contact a CA or notify an owner.
limitations: Pending operation metadata is not a complete renewal attempt history.
Vault firewall or certificate data plane denial leaves renewal status unassessed; Activity Log does not reveal certificate private key or secret reads.

title: Defender for Cloud assessment
description: Use when investigating defender for cloud assessment. Assess current Defender for Cloud recommendations and secure score, separating verified changes from unavailable history.
analysis: Report current score by initiative and subscription, preserving its maximum and percentage. Do not average subscription percentages without an explicit weighting rule.
Group Unhealthy assessed resources by metadata severity; count distinct resource IDs per recommendation, then rank the top ten by impacted count. Missing severity is unknown, not Low.

Compute 30 day trend only from comparable retained samples. Mark seven day additions as first observed since a complete earlier snapshot, not as proof of creation. Without earlier evidence, both trend and new recommendation count are null.
Prioritize known exploitability evidence and approved dependency or exposure inventory. Distinguish recommendation severity from confirmed exploitability and actual workload blast radius.
limitations: Current assessment listing is not a 30 day history API.
Continuous export coverage and retention can be incomplete; absence of a recommendation from a failed snapshot is not remediation.
